title: Tenant reservoirs: capacity safeguards, adaptive autoscale, and graceful fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
background: As Dedicated customers scale, transient tenant spikes and maintenance events lead to unpredictable latencies and failed requests. Current reserved reservations and burst heuristics are brittle: some tenants exhaust credits quickly while others underutilize allocations. We need a more fluid per-tenant mechanism that smooths burst demand, reduces failed requests, and retains predictable economics for committed capacity.
problem_statement: Large tenant bursts cause cascading queueing and preemption, hurting latency SLOs for critical tenants and complicating on-call. Existing soft-reserve and fairshare features are not responsive enough to short spikes and lack clear fallback behavior when capacity is exhausted. We also lack a predictable, testable policy for temporarily expanding capacity in safe, billable ways.
goals: 1) Introduce a per-tenant 'reservoir' of soft capacity credits that accrues and decays based on historical usage; 2) Provide an adaptive autoscaler that can temporarily provision controlled burst capacity (prewarm) for short windows; 3) Define deterministic graceful fallback chains (quantized model, shared pool, queued retry) so requests fail less often and with predictable behavior; 4) Expose clear observability and billing signals for tenant-level usage of extra capacity.
non_goals: 1) This PRD does not change tenant billing model for long-term committed capacity; 2) Not implementing full multi-region failover; 3) Not replacing Dedicated's existing long-running reservation purchase flow.
success_metrics:
- 95th percentile token generation latency for tenants using reservoirs improved or unchanged under burst load (target: <= existing baseline +5%)
- Burst-induced request failures reduced by >= 80% for targeted tenants during controlled load tests
- Fallback execution success (requests completed via fallback path) >= 99% when primary capacity unavailable
- Cost delta for the platform when enabling adaptive prewarm on canary tenants <= +10% compared to baseline
- Observability: per-tenant reservoir usage showable in Console (dashboard + API) and billing reconciliation matches usage logs within 24 hours
requirements: Reservoir model: per-tenant soft credit bucket that accrues at a configurable rate and decays; credits consumed per request proportional to estimated token cost
Configurable reservoir policies per-tenant and per-project (accrual rate, max capacity, decay half-life)
Adaptive autoscaler: ability to request short-lived prewarm capacity from Dedicated pools with bounds (minutes, GPUs, per-tenant cap)
Fallback chains: declarative per-tenant fallback policies with ordered steps (e.g., prefix cache hit -> quantized model -> shared burst pool -> queue+retry)
Instrumentation: expose metrics (reservoir_balance, reservoir_consumption_rate, prewarm_allocations, fallback_invocations, fallback_success_rate) in Console and as Prometheus metrics
Policy enforcement: deterministic admission control that reads reservoir state and enforces per-request decisions with audit logging
Console UX: UI to view/override reservoir settings and to visualize historical credit usage and fallback events
APIs/SDKs: endpoints to query reservoir balance and to request/pre-authorize prewarm as part of request lifecycle
Load testing harness and synthetic tenants to validate behavior under varied spike patterns
Safety limits: global rate-limits for prewarm to prevent runaway cost; automatic backoff if prewarm error rates or sustained overload detected
constraints:
- Implementation must work within existing Dedicated orchestration primitives (no infra rework).
- Prewarm capacity must be billable and auditable.
- Changes must not reduce existing tenant isolation guarantees.
- Console/observability changes must fit within current telemetry retention limits (adjustments to retention may be a follow-on).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for reservoir accounting logic with edge cases (zero accrual, negative balance, concurrent consumption)
Integration test where a synthetic tenant performs a 5-minute spike (10x baseline RPS): reservoir + adaptive autoscale must limit failed requests to <1% across 3 runs
Fallback chain exercised in integration tests; at least two fallback steps succeed in completing requests when primary path is unavailable
Canary rollout (5% of tenants): prewarm allocation capped and monitored for cost delta; no SLO regressions observed for other tenants in the same pool
Console surfaces per-tenant reservoir balance, prewarm events, and a link to billing reconciliation logs
Operational runbook added: step-by-step playbook for identifying reservoir exhaustion, revoking prewarm, and rolling back policies
Performance: end-to-end critical path added decision latency < 2ms at median and < 10ms at P95 for admission checks under normal load
rollout_plan: 1) Dev + unit tests (2 weeks) -> 2) Integration feature branch with synthetic tenants (2 weeks) -> 3) Internal dogfood on non-production Dedicated env (1 week) -> 4) Canary launch to 5% low-risk tenants with feature flag (2 weeks) -> 5) Monitor metrics and iterate -> 6) Gradual ramp to 50% then GA after verification. Each stage gated by SLOs and cost checks.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New dashboards: 'Tenant Reservoirs Overview' and 'Adaptive Prewarm Usage'
- Alerts: reservoir_depletion_rate > threshold for N tenants in 5m; prewarm_failure_rate > 5% sustained for 10m; fallback_success_rate < 98% over 30m
- On-call playbook: automated ticket creation with links to top offending tenants and quick rollback toggle
migration_strategy: Existing tenants start with a conservative default reservoir policy (low accrual, small max). Admins can opt-in higher tiers. Provide a migration script to map current soft-reserve and fairshare settings to initial reservoir parameters. For tenants using custom reservations, we will run a consulting-assisted migration path.
security_and_compliance_notes: No new PII introduced. Audit logs for admission decisions and prewarm allocations must be capturable by existing KMS/HSM and audit pipelines. Ensure RBAC controls restrict who can override reservoir policies in Console.
open_questions: What is the default accrual formula for new tenants (flat rate vs usage-proportional)?
How should we bill prewarm allocations if prewarm is requested but unused? (charge full vs pro-rated)
Priority mapping: how do enterprise SLA tiers map to reservoir weight/priority during contention?
Should we permit cross-tenant borrowing inside the same customer organization (org-level reservoir)?
